For your heart is still not softened — has not yet become compassionate. That Vrishabhanu's daughter Radha keeps an illicit bond with you — this I am enduring within my own heart. Such is the grace [I have described] of yours. We Nagars are reckoned truly plain-spoken people, and whatever we happen to say, good or ill, we give no thought to it. Without you, at whose feet shall we take refuge? Therefore your devotee Narsinh Mehta has become angry. He says: without me, who will sing your praises? Without you, who else will come to my aid?)

Thus, the pad "We had gone to Mathura to sell curd," sung by Narsinh Mehta, was sung by Narsinh Mehta even before Jivanji Maharaj's own arrival, in anticipation of Jivanji Maharaj's manifestation itself. Thus Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj had appeared in order to deliver Bhoja Gurjar.

====000====

Krishna Darshan

Shyamdasji, who set down in words the life-story of Sadguru Shri Jivanji Maharaj, has described many aspects of his life. He has given a beautiful account of just such an incident. Once, among Jivanji Maharaj's own devotees (nij jan), there was an exceedingly pure, love-drenched, singularly devoted, unique woman devotee, all on her own; a certain thought kept coming to her mind again and again. Many thoughts about her own Sadguru Shri Jivanji Maharaj kept arising in this very innocent (bhali) woman devotee's mind. Having found so great a philosopher-sage, so singular a Sadguru, this woman devotee had become deeply moved. Moreover, seeing so beautiful a social order and arrangement, thoughts would arise in this sister's mind: who could such a great saintly person really be? Who could this Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj really be, who has spread so beautiful and so lofty a stream of thought throughout Gujarat? On this question, many thoughts kept arising. Once, sinking deep into such thoughts, this innocent woman devotee entered a state of loving trance (bhaav samadhi) and had a beautiful vision. Sadguru Shri Jivanji Maharaj told her in that dream: "O innocent sister! When I lie down to sleep, come then to see me."

As soon as she had this beautiful experience, this innocent woman awoke from her loving trance, and at once went to the room where Jivanji Maharaj lay sleeping. She lifted the cloth covering that lay over the face and head of the sleeping Jivanji Maharaj to look, and was struck with wonder. She beheld the form of the Complete Brahman (Purna Brahman) — the Supreme Being, wearing a peacock crown and yellow silk garments (pitambar). Beholding the flute-bearing Lord, radiant as a crore of suns, this sister began to feel most blessed. She fixed this form firmly in her heart, and all her doubts and misgivings were dispelled, and she began to worship with ever-increasing love and devotion.
